references.text: Abraham calls himself a stranger and sojourner among the Hittites – this uses the same terminology as Jacob's words about his own and his fathers' years of wandering (מְגוּרַי / מְגוּרֵיהֶם).
Abraham lived 175 years. Jacob says that his 130 years do not reach the days of his fathers – Abraham lived 45 years longer than Jacob was at this point.
Isaac lived 180 years, which confirms Jacob's statement that his own years (130 at this time) did not reach those of his fathers.
Jacob lived a total of 147 years – 17 of them in Egypt. This confirms that he was 130 years old when he met Pharaoh, which matches his statement in v.9.

David says in his prayer: 'We are strangers and sojourners before you, as all our fathers; like a shadow are our days on the earth.' A direct parallel to Jacob's reflection on life as a pilgrimage journey.
The psalmist prays: 'I am a stranger with you, a foreigner like all my fathers' – almost a word-for-word echo of Jacob's words about his years of wandering compared to those of his fathers.
Hebrews refers to the patriarchs as strangers and foreigners on earth who lived by faith. This provides a theological framework for Jacob's description of life as a pilgrimage journey.
Jacob's confirmation that his life fulfills God's prophecy in 15:13 about alienation and oppression.
Highlights the connection between the family's identity as 'shepherds' (47:3) and their status as 'strangers' with hard years (47:9).
